question: A build script wants to pipe a large build-error log into Claude for a root-cause explanation: cat build-error.txt | claude -p 'explain the root cause' > output.txt. On one particularly verbose failure, the job exits immediately with an error and no explanation is produced. What is the most likely cause given how Claude Code handles piped stdin?
options: A) The redirect operator > is not supported when combined with -p, so the shell discarded the response before Claude could write it
B) The build log exceeded the 10MB cap on piped stdin, so Claude Code exited with an error instead of processing the oversized input
C) The build log contained non-UTF8 bytes, which -p mode rejects outright regardless of file size
D) Piped stdin is only accepted when --input-format stream-json is explicitly set, so plain text piping silently failed
correct_answers: B) The build log exceeded the 10MB cap on piped stdin, so Claude Code exited with an error instead of processing the oversized input
explanations: Standard shell output redirection works normally with -p mode; there is no special restriction preventing '>' from capturing Claude Code's output.

Correct. Piped stdin in Claude Code is capped at 10MB; exceeding it causes the CLI to exit with a clear error and non-zero status rather than processing the content. The documented workaround is to write the content to a file and reference the path in the prompt instead.
The described stdin limitation in Claude Code's documentation is a size cap, not a character-encoding restriction; an encoding issue is not the documented failure mode here.
Plain text stdin piping is the default and documented pattern for -p mode; --input-format stream-json is only needed for the stream-json input/output pairing, not for ordinary piped text.
